claims.text: App-delivered sleep therapy reproduces selected elements of therapist-guided CBT-I and can retain partial efficacy, but it may lack individualization and accountability.
Reported effects of digital sleep interventions vary widely across studies, limiting strong conclusions about durability.
Structured CBT-I improves sleep onset latency in adults, with benefits observed at six-month follow-up, although adherence may decline among shift workers.
Digital sleep therapy is best understood as a scalable delivery model that requires longer trials and better adherence reporting before equivalence to therapist-guided care can be assumed.
